concepts.learning_objective: Explain why our sense of touch cannot always correctly judge whether a body is hot or cold.
Predict how the same water feels to hands that were earlier kept in warm and in cold water.
State that temperature is a reliable measure of the hotness or coldness of a body and compare bodies by it.
Identify a thermometer as the device for measuring temperature and distinguish clinical from laboratory thermometers by use.
Describe the digital clinical thermometer and why it has replaced the mercury thermometer.
List the steps and precautions for measuring body temperature with a digital clinical thermometer.
Interpret normal body temperature as an average and relate armpit readings to actual body temperature.
Name the Celsius, Fahrenheit and Kelvin scales, their units and the SI unit of temperature.
Convert a temperature from the Celsius scale to the Kelvin scale.
Write temperatures and their unit symbols correctly.

topics.title: Laboratory thermometer: range and smallest value

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the parts of a laboratory thermometer and its usual range.
Calculate the smallest value a thermometer can read and use it to take a reading.

topics.title: Measuring temperature with a laboratory thermometer

concepts.learning_objective: Follow the correct way of measuring the temperature of water with a laboratory thermometer.
Recognise that water stays at a constant temperature while boiling and ice while melting.
Interpret maximum and minimum air temperatures from weather reports and their use in forecasts.
Recall Anna Mani's contribution to weather measurement instruments in India.
